YEARLY PHYSICAL - 56M

No new problems. Neck stiff mornings, no arm symptoms since 2024. Low back and knees: same pattern, worse after double shifts. Ibuprofen on work days. Sleeps OK. PHQ-2 1, a tired week, nothing more.

Exam: BP as charted. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abd benign. Neck: rotation mildly limited, Spurling negative. Arms 5/5, reflexes symmetric. Knees crepitus, no effusion. Back: well-healed scar, nontender.

Plan
- HTN: controlled on lisinopril 10.
- Spine and knees: stable, home exercises.
- CMP and lipids today. Flu today; he'll get his COVID booster at the pharmacy. Lung CT in November, ordered. Colonoscopy due 2029.
RTC 6 months.

CERVICAL SPINE RADIOGRAPHS
Indication: right arm weakness and numbness after lifting.
Findings: Alignment normal, no listhesis. No fracture. Degenerative changes with disc space narrowing and osteophyte formation in the lower cervical spine. Prevertebral soft tissues normal.
reports.conclusion: Degenerative changes of the cervical spine with disc space narrowing and osteophytes. No acute osseous abnormality.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PHYSICIAN RECORD
Arrival: 12/28/2025 10:40

CC: right arm weakness and numbness x 2 weeks.

HPI: 57M, warehouse loader, symptoms in the right arm since lifting a run of heavy boxes overhead at work about two weeks ago. Hard to grip; weakness worse squeezing hard or shoving doors open. Tingling runs from the shoulder along the back of the arm and forearm into the middle finger. Turning his head to the right or looking up for a while brings it on. Had a similar problem on the left side in July 2024, seen by PM&R and treated with therapy. Came today because he could not hold a coffee mug steady this morning. No bowel or bladder change, no leg symptoms, no fever.

PMH: cervical spondylosis with multilevel DDD C5-C6, C6-C7; cervical radiculopathy; hypertension; mechanical low back pain; bilateral knee OA.
PSH: L4-L5 lumbar laminectomy 2022; left rotator cuff repair 2016.
Meds: ibuprofen 600 mg TID PRN; cyclobenzaprine 5 mg QHS PRN; lisinopril 10 mg daily; acetaminophen 500 mg PRN.
Allergies: sulfa (urticaria), shellfish.
FH: father cervical spondylosis with myelopathy, HTN; mother OA, osteoporosis; brother cervical radiculopathy s/p ACDF.
SH: former smoker, 20 pack-years, quit 2019. Weekend beers.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet. Uncomfortable but nontoxic. Neck: Spurling's maneuver reproduces the right arm symptoms. Triceps reflex decreased on the right compared with the left; biceps and brachioradialis symmetric. Strength reduced in right wrist extension and elbow extension; shoulder abduction and finger abduction full. Pinprick diminished over the right posterior forearm and the back of the third finger. Left arm normal. Legs: strength, sensation and reflexes normal, no clonus, gait normal.

Imaging: C-spine x-ray with degenerative narrowing and osteophytes, nothing acute.

MDM: radicular deficit in a right C7 distribution without myelopathic signs or red flags. Outpatient MRI appropriate.

Diagnosis: compression of the right C7 nerve root; cervical radiculopathy.

Disposition: discharged home 14:10. Continue home ibuprofen and cyclobenzaprine as needed. Avoid overhead lifting. Follow up with primary care within one week for outpatient MRI and specialist referral. Return for worsening weakness, leg symptoms, or bladder or bowel problems.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Post-ED visit. Seen 12/28 for right arm weakness and numbness after overhead lifting mid-December; ED found a right C7 picture, x-ray degenerative only, sent home on his usual meds.

Since then: tingling down the back of the right arm into the middle finger a little less constant. Grip still weak, drops things now and then. Neck sore looking up. No left arm or leg symptoms, bladder and bowels normal. Ibuprofen twice a day, cyclobenzaprine at night. Pain 5/10.

Exam: BP as charted. Right triceps reflex reduced vs left. Right elbow and wrist extension 4/5. Shoulder abduction and finger abduction 5/5. Pinprick reduced on the back of the right forearm and third finger. Spurling positive on the right. Left arm and legs normal, gait normal.

A/P: Right C7 radiculopathy, motor deficit present but not worse. MRI C-spine ordered and PM&R referral (same group as 2024). Same PRN meds. Work note: no overhead lifting and nothing over 20 lb for 4 weeks. ED precautions reviewed.

reports.text:
MRI CERVICAL SPINE WITHOUT CONTRAST
Indication: right arm weakness and paresthesias in a C7 distribution.
Comparison: 6/26/2024.
Findings: Alignment maintained. No fracture or marrow abnormality. Cord normal in caliber and signal throughout.
C5-C6: disc desiccation and height loss with degenerative bulge, without canal or foraminal compromise. Unchanged.
C6-C7: disc desiccation and height loss. Right foraminal disc herniation compresses the exiting right C7 nerve root. Left foramen patent. No cord compression.
Other levels without significant stenosis.
reports.conclusion:
1. Right foraminal C6-C7 disc herniation compressing the right C7 nerve root.
2. Known multilevel degenerative disc disease at C5-C6 and C6-C7.
3. No cord compression.

documents.title: MRI
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: The MRI shows a disc at C6-C7 pushing on the right-side nerve root, which matches your symptoms. The left side that bothered you in 2024 looks open now, and the spinal cord is fine. PM&R has you on 1/21. Keep the work restrictions until then.

documents.title: Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation Consultation
documents.author: physiatry
documents.body:
PM&R CONSULTATION
Date of visit: 01/21/2026
Referred for: right arm weakness and paresthesias.

Known to this clinic from 2024 for left cervical radiculopathy that resolved with therapy. Since mid-December, after overhead lifting at work, weakness and tingling in the right arm along the back of the arm into the middle finger. ED 12/28. Slowly improving, on modified duty.

Meds: lisinopril 10 mg daily; ibuprofen 600 mg TID PRN; cyclobenzaprine 5 mg QHS PRN; acetaminophen 500 mg PRN. Allergies: sulfa, shellfish.

Exam: Right triceps reflex reduced. Right elbow extension and wrist extension 4/5, otherwise full strength. Pinprick decreased over the dorsal right forearm and third digit. Spurling positive right. No Hoffmann sign, gait normal. Left arm normal.

MRI 1/12/2026: right foraminal C6-C7 herniation compressing the right C7 root.

Impression: right C7 radiculopathy from C6-C7 foraminal disc herniation, on multilevel cervical spondylosis.

Plan:
- Physical therapy, referral placed.
- Continue light duty: no overhead work, 20 lb limit.
- Ibuprofen and cyclobenzaprine as needed.
- If not clearly better in 6 to 8 weeks, consider a cervical epidural steroid injection or a spine surgery opinion.
- Follow-up in about 10 weeks.

documents.title: Physical Therapy Initial Evaluation
documents.author: physical therapy
documents.body:
PT EVALUATION 1/27/2026
Dx: right C7 radiculopathy.
Returning patient (left-sided episode 2024). Right arm tingling to the middle finger, weak grip at work.
Objective: cervical extension and right rotation limited and reproduce arm symptoms. Right triceps 4/5, wrist extensors 4/5. Pinprick reduced dorsal forearm and third finger.
Plan: 2x/week x 8 weeks: traction trial, nerve mobility, deep neck flexor and scapular strengthening, return-to-lift progression, home program.
